- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
1	# SprintHub
2	
3	**Your GitHub sprint board and PR hub — right inside VS Code.**
4	
5	Stop switching between VS Code and the browser 30 times a day. SprintHub brings your GitHub Projects v2 board, pull request statuses, CI results, and sprint progress into a single panel where you already work.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Why SprintHub?
10	
11	Most teams manage their sprint in GitHub Projects and their code in VS Code — but checking issue status, reviewing PRs, and tracking CI means constantly jumping to the browser. SprintHub closes that gap.
12	
13	- ✅ See your full sprint board without leaving VS Code
14	- ✅ Know instantly which PRs need your attention
15	- ✅ Track CI pass/fail per PR at a glance
16	- ✅ Filter everything by sprint in one click
17	- ✅ Stays in sync — auto-refreshes in the background
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Features
22	
23	### 🚀 Dashboard (main tab)
24	A high-signal PR hub that shows exactly what needs action. Every open pull request — including PRs linked to board issues — grouped by status:
25	
26	| Group | What it means |
27	|---|---|
28	| **Ready to Merge** | Approved + all checks passing — just needs a merge |
29	| **Changes Requested** | A reviewer asked for changes |
30	| **CI Failing** | One or more checks are red |
31	| **Ready for Review** | Awaiting a reviewer |
32	| **Needs Review** | No one assigned to review yet |
33	| **In Progress** | Actively being worked on |
34	| **Draft** | Not ready for review yet |
35	
36	**"Assigned to me" filter** — one click to see only PRs you authored, are assigned to, or are requested to review.
37	
38	### 📋 Main Board
39	Full Kanban view of your GitHub Project v2. Filter by sprint, search by keyword, click any item to read its full description and comments — all without opening a browser tab.
40	
41	### 🏁 Milestones
42	Browse all milestones and drill into the issues attached to each one.
43	
44	### ⚙️ Settings
45	Configure everything from inside the extension. No digging through VS Code settings JSON.
46	
47	---
48	
49	## Setup (takes 2 minutes)
50	
51	1. Install SprintHub
52	2. Click the **SprintHub icon** in the VS Code activity bar
53	3. Click **Open SprintHub**
54	4. Click the **⚙️ icon** (top-right) to open Settings
55	5. Enter:
56	   - **Owner** — your GitHub org or username
57	   - **Project number** — the number in your GitHub Project URL (`/projects/42` → `42`)
58	   - **Owner type** — Organization or User
59	6. Hit Save — your board loads instantly
60	
61	> SprintHub uses your existing VS Code GitHub authentication. No extra login required.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Requirements
66	
67	- VS Code 1.85 or newer
68	- GitHub account signed in through VS Code
69	- A [GitHub Project v2](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/about-projects) (classic Projects v1 are not supported)
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Settings Reference
74	
75	| Setting | Default | Description |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| `sprinthub.owner` | `""` | GitHub org or username |
78	| `sprinthub.projectNumber` | `0` | GitHub Project v2 number |
79	| `sprinthub.ownerType` | `"organization"` | `"organization"` or `"user"` |
80	| `sprinthub.statusFieldName` | `"Status"` | Name of your board's status field |
81	| `sprinthub.refreshInterval` | `5` | Auto-refresh in minutes (0 = off) |
82	| `sprinthub.colorBlind` | `false` | Replaces red/green with orange/blue |
83	| `sprinthub.liquidGlass` | `false` | Frosted-glass UI style |
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Tips
88	
89	**Sprint filter** — select a sprint in the toolbar to filter the board and dashboard simultaneously.
90	
91	**Linked PRs** — the Dashboard finds PRs linked to your board issues even when the PR itself isn't on the board. Works with `Fixes #N`, `Closes #N`, `Resolves #N` in the PR body.
92	
93	**CI dots** — each PR row shows a colored dot: 🟢 passing, 🔴 failing, 🟡 pending, ⚪ no CI.
94	
95	**Color-blind mode** — enable in Settings to replace all red/green signals with orange/blue.
96	
97	---
98	
99	## Privacy
100	
101	SprintHub reads data exclusively from GitHub using your VS Code GitHub session token. No data is sent to any third-party service. All requests go directly to `api.github.com`.
102	
103	---
104	
105	## Feedback
106	
107	Found a bug or have a feature idea? [Open an issue](https://github.com/gaelrobin/sprinthub/issues) — contributions welcome!
108

---

## SprintHub VS Code Extension - Structural Overview

### 1. **Top-Level Directory Layout**

```
/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/extension/SprintHub/
├── src/                          # Extension backend (TypeScript)
├── webview-ui/                   # React frontend (TypeScript + React)
├── out/                          # Compiled output (esbuild)
├── resources/                    # Assets (icons, SVGs)
├── .vscode/                      # VS Code workspace config
├── .github/                      # GitHub workflows/actions
├── .claude/                      # Claude Code config
├── node_modules/                 # Dependencies
├── esbuild.js                    # Build configuration
├── package.json                  # Project metadata & scripts
├── tsconfig.json                 # TypeScript config
├── tsconfig.webview.json         # Separate TS config for webview
├── .eslintrc.json                # Linting rules
└── README.md                     # Documentation
```

---

### 2. **Key Source Files**

#### **Backend (Extension) — `/src` (1,088 lines total)**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| **extension.ts** | Entry point; registers the `sprinthub.open` command and sidebar tree provider |
| **SprintHubPanel.ts** | Manages the webview panel lifecycle, message routing, config updates, data loading, and auto-refresh |
| **githubService.ts** | All GitHub GraphQL API calls; fetches project data, linked PRs, check runs, and item bodies |
| **types.ts** | TypeScript interfaces for: `BoardItem`, `RunwayData`, `RunwayConfig`, `LinkedPR`, `CheckRun`, message types |

#### **Frontend (Webview UI) — `/webview-ui` (3,324 lines total)**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| **App.tsx** | Main React component; manages global state (data, config, filters, detail panel), routing between tabs, and styling (dark/light themes, liquid glass, color-blind mode) |
| **index.tsx** | ReactDOM entry point; renders the App into the `#root` div |
| **components/ColumnGroup.tsx** | Renders a single Kanban column with collapsible header, item count, and list of `ItemCard` components |
| **components/ItemCard.tsx** | Displays a single board item (issue or PR) with type icon, title, labels, assignees, CI status, branch name, diff stats |
| **components/DetailPanel.tsx** | Right-side overlay showing full item details, linked PRs (for issues), check runs, review status, metadata (author, milestone, sprint) |
| **components/LaunchpadView.tsx** | Dashboard view grouping PRs by status ("Ready to Merge", "CI Failing", "Changes Requested", etc.); shows action-priority PRs |
| **components/SettingsPanel.tsx** | Modal for configuring owner, project number, status field name, refresh interval, themes, color-blind mode |

---

### 3. **Existing Features**

#### **Core Functionality**
- **GitHub Projects v2 Dashboard** — Full Kanban board synced from GitHub
- **PR Hub (Launchpad)** — Smart grouping of PRs by action needed (approved → merge, CI failing, awaiting review, etc.)
- **Sprint Filtering** — Dropdown to filter all items by iteration/sprint
- **Search** — Full-text search across title, number, author, labels, branch, sprint, milestone
- **Auto-refresh** — Background polling every N minutes (configurable: 0–60 min)

#### **Item Details**
- **Detail Panel** — Click any item to see full description, assignees, labels, milestone, sprint
- **Linked PRs** — For issues, fetches all PRs that reference it via `Fixes #N` syntax
- **Check Runs** — Shows CI pipeline status per PR (name, status, conclusion, link to details)
- **Review Status** — Displays approved/changes-requested/pending counts

#### **UI Modes & Settings**
- **Dark/Light Theme** — Toggle between Catppuccin Mocha (dark) and Latte (light)
- **Liquid Glass** — Frosted-glass estheticUI style with backdrop blur
- **Color-Blind Mode** — Replaces red/green signals (CI pass/fail, review status) with orange/blue (deuteranopia-safe)
- **Configurable Columns** — Auto-detected project status field; defaults to "Status"
- **Multiple Project Types** — Supports both organization and user-owned projects

#### **Views/Tabs**
1. **Dashboard** — PR-centric, groups by action priority
2. **Main Board** — Traditional Kanban with columns
3. **Pull Requests** — Filters board to only PRs
4. **Issues** — Filters board to only issues
5. **Milestones** — Groups all items by milestone

### 5. **GitHub API Integration & Git Utilities**

#### **GitHub GraphQL API Usage**

**Primary Queries:**
- **`PROJECT_ITEMS_QUERY`** — Fetches all items from a GitHub Project v2, with pagination; supports both org and user-owned projects; includes issue/PR metadata, assignees, labels, milestones, CI status, reviews
- **`REPO_OPEN_PRS_QUERY`** — For each repo on the board, fetches all open PRs to find ones linked to board issues (via `closingIssuesReferences`)
- **`LINKED_PRS_QUERY`** — Finds PRs linked to a specific issue via `closingPullRequests` and timeline cross-references
- **`ITEM_BODY_QUERY`** — Fetches the full markdown body of an issue or PR (loaded on demand, not in bulk)

**REST API Usage:**
- **Check Runs endpoint** — `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs` to fetch CI/workflow results per PR

#### **Authentication**
- Uses **VS Code's built-in GitHub authentication** via `vscode.authentication.getSession('github', [...])`
- Scopes requested: `repo`, `read:org`, `read:user`, `project`
- Token is automatically managed by VS Code; no manual token storage

#### **Key Data Structures**

**BoardItem** (src/types.ts, lines 43–71)
- Represents any item on the board (issue or PR)
- Fields: `id`, `number`, `title`, `type`, `column`, `state`, `author`, `assignees`, `labels`, `repository`, `ciState`, `reviews`, etc.
- PR-only fields: `isDraft`, `additions`, `deletions`, `headRefName`, `reviewRequests`, `closingIssueNumbers`

**LinkedPR** (src/types.ts, lines 27–36)
- Represents a PR linked to a board issue
- Fields: `number`, `title`, `url`, `state`, `isDraft`, `headRefName`, `ciState`, `checkRuns`

**RunwayData** (src/types.ts, lines 73–83)
- The full project snapshot
- Fields: `projectTitle`, `columns` (ordered), `groups` (items by column), `sprints`, `linkedIssuePRs`, `lastUpdated`, `totalCount`

### 6. **Architecture Summary**

```
GitHub (GraphQL API)
        ↓
    githubService.ts
        ↓
    SprintHubPanel.ts (webview ↔ extension message bridge)
        ↓
    App.tsx (React state: data, filters, detail panel)
        ├── LaunchpadView (Dashboard tab)
        ├── ColumnGroup[] (Main Board, Milestones tabs)
        ├── DetailPanel (Right overlay)
        └── SettingsPanel (Modal)
```

**Message Flow:**
- **Extension → Webview:** `{ type: 'data'|'config'|'linkedPRs'|'itemBody'|'error'|'loading', ... }`
- **Webview → Extension:** `{ type: 'refresh'|'updateConfig'|'fetchLinkedPRs'|'fetchBody'|'openUrl'|'getConfig' }`
